title: A quiet five minutes
line: The oldest shape there is: adore, admit, thank, ask. Four turns, five minutes.

steps.label: Adore
steps.prompt: Say one true thing about who God is. Not what he has done for you — who he is.

steps.label: Admit
steps.prompt: Name one thing plainly, without explaining why it happened. He already knows the context.

steps.label: Thank
steps.prompt: Three things from the last day. Small ones count, and they are usually the honest ones.

steps.label: Ask
steps.prompt: Ask for what you actually want, in the words you would use to a friend.

steps.label: Stay
steps.prompt: Say nothing for a moment. This is the part everyone skips.

title: When you are anxious
line: For a mind that is running the same loop. Move it out of your head and into a sentence.

steps.label: Name it
steps.prompt: What exactly are you afraid will happen? Say the specific thing, not the mood.

steps.label: Separate
steps.prompt: Which part of this is yours to do this week, and which part is not yours at all?

steps.label: Hand over
steps.prompt: Ask God for the part that is not yours. Use the word 'please'.

steps.label: Thank
steps.prompt: Name one thing that went right recently. Anxiety has a short memory.

steps.label: Breathe
steps.prompt: Sit still and breathe slowly. Peace is promised as a guard, not as a feeling you produce.

title: Before the shift
line: Four minutes before you clock in, for the hours you are about to spend.

steps.label: Offer
steps.prompt: Give the next eight hours to God out loud, before anyone asks anything of you.

steps.label: The people
steps.prompt: Name the person at work who is hardest to be around. Ask for something good for them.

steps.label: The temptation
steps.prompt: You know where you will be tempted to cut a corner today. Ask for help there specifically.

steps.label: The witness
steps.prompt: Ask that something about today makes somebody curious.

title: For the people at home
line: For a family in another time zone, prayed for by name.

steps.label: Name them
steps.prompt: Say each name out loud. One at a time, not as a group.

steps.label: What you cannot do
steps.prompt: Tell God the thing you would fix if you were there. Ask him to do it.

steps.label: The distance
steps.prompt: Say honestly what being away costs you. Do not tidy it up.

steps.label: Provision
steps.prompt: Pray for what you send and how it is used, without anxiety about the amount.

steps.label: Bless
steps.prompt: Ask God to be to them today what you cannot be.

title: Before you sleep
line: The examen, plainly: look back over the day with God before you close it.

steps.label: Replay
steps.prompt: Walk back through the day from waking. Do not judge it yet — just watch it.

steps.label: Where he was
steps.prompt: Where was God in it? Name the moment you would otherwise have called luck.

steps.label: Where you were not
steps.prompt: Name one thing you would do differently. Once, and without a speech.

steps.label: Leave it
steps.prompt: Hand tomorrow over. Anything still open can be open in his hands rather than yours.

title: When you have no words
line: For grief, exhaustion, or a day when praying feels like acting. Almost nothing is asked of you here.

steps.label: Sit
steps.prompt: You do not have to say anything yet. Sit for a moment and let that be allowed.

steps.label: One word
steps.prompt: If one word comes — help, or tired, or please — say only that.

steps.label: Hear
steps.prompt: Read the verse above slowly, twice. Let it be said to you rather than by you.

steps.label: Stay
steps.prompt: Stay a little longer than is comfortable. Nothing more is required of you today.
